THE map on the left-hand page is NOT jus
I an artist's conception of proposed post
war air routes. Quite the contrary! It shows
a world-wide system of over 98,000 miles that
was actually in operation before Pearl Harbor.
This, the world's greatest air transport system,
was carrying international passengers, mail,
air cargo and the United States flag to five con-
tinents as long ago as 1941.
MORE THAN THAT!
Most of the routes pioneered by Pan American
World Airways before the war have been in con-
tinuous operation ever since... Many of them, in
co-operation and under contract with the Army
Air Transport Command and the Navy Air
Transport Service, have been greatly extended.
Service to Wake Island, Guam, Manila, Hong
Kong and New Zealand may be temporarily
discontinued but Hawaii, Africa, Portugal, Ire-
land and all the leading cities of Latin America
are still regular ports of call for giant Clippers
on scheduled flight.
Look at the solid lines in the large map
(left). If you have need today to fly to any of
the cities on those routes, please consult your
local Pan American office or your own travel
agent. They will be glad to give you schedules,
rates, and other information. For Air Express
shipments, telephone Railway Express Agency.
